# Using Option Groups in PDF Template Layouts

Option groups let one PDF layout work across several film products, even when those products use different option keys on the order.

For example, your 35mm, black-and-white and 120 film products might arrive with these keys:

* `scanning-35mm`
* `scanning-bw`
* `scanning-120`

If you assign all three to the group **scanning**, a single line on your job ticket can print the scanning choice for any of them. Without groups you would need a separate layout, or a separate line, for every key.

This article covers both halves of the job: setting the group up in **Option Display**, and using it in a layout. How you set it up decides what you can print.

---

## Step 1 — Put your options into a group

1. Go to **Settings → Organization → Film Development → Option Display**.
2. Select the pencil icon on an option, or add the option if it is not listed yet.
3. Fill in **Group**. This is the shared name your layouts will use, for example `scanning`, `develop` or `prints`.
4. Repeat for every option key that means the same thing, giving them all the **same** Group.
5. Save.

* Note: Group names ignore capital letters and spaces around them. Keep them short, lower case and consistent — `scanning`, not `Scanning Options`.
* Note: Group is optional. An option with no Group still shows on the Scanning Station; it simply cannot be printed with a group token.

![Scanning Options Table](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/210465a4-402b-432f-b483-6b5abcd06d07.png)

---

## Step 2 — Decide what each value should print

An option group can print three different things, and each comes from a different field in **Option Display**:

| What you want on the ticket | Where it comes from | Token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The friendly value wording, e.g. "High resolution" | **Label shown** on the value label | `{option_group:scanning}` |
| The heading, e.g. "Scanning" | **Title shown** on the option, or **Title shown for this value** if that value overrides it | `{option_group_title:scanning}` |
| Both, e.g. "Scanning - High resolution" | Both of the above | `{option_group_full:scanning}` |

This is the tie-up between setup and layout: if you never set **Label shown** for a value, `{option_group:scanning}` prints the raw order wording instead. If you want tidy tickets, add a value label for every value your products actually send.

* Note: **Title shown for this value** is powerful here. It lets one group print a different heading depending on what the customer chose — for example "Scan at 6000 × 4000 px" instead of the generic "Scanning".

---

## Step 3 — Add the group to your layout

1. Open **Settings → Organization → PDF Designer** and edit the layout.
2. Add or select a text element.
3. In the properties panel find **Option group (from Option Display)**.
4. Choose the group from the list, or type it in the **Or type a group (e.g. scanning)** box.
5. Choose what to print:
   * **Print the friendly label**
   * **Print the title**
   * **Print label and title**
   * **Print my own text when it matches**
6. Select **Insert token**. The token drops into the text element where your cursor is.

![Option Group](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/daa5bfa4-4e3d-4e6e-a2e1-9838f779afcb.png)

---

## Step 4 — Printing your own text (conditions)

**Print my own text when it matches** builds a condition. You choose **is** or **is not**, type a value, and give the text to print for each outcome.

Typical film examples:

```
{?option_group:scanning!=none:SCAN WEB:}
{?option_group:develop!=none:DEVELOP:}
{?option_group:prints!=none:PRINT:}
```

Each line prints its word only when that group has a real choice on the job — a simple work-to-do checklist at the top of the ticket.

You can also switch between two pieces of text:

```
{?option_group:scanning=high-res:HIGH RES SCAN:STANDARD SCAN}
```

* The comparison matches the **raw order value or the friendly label**, so either works.
* Capital letters and spaces are ignored.
* Either piece of text can be left empty.

---

## Step 5 — What "none" means

`none` is the value to use when you want to ask "did the customer choose anything here?".

A group counts as **none** when:

* the job has no option in that group at all, or
* the value is empty, or
* the value or its label is a "not chosen" wording.

Recognised "not chosen" wordings include:

`none`, `no`, `n/a`, `nil`, `false`, `0`, `off`, `no scan`, `no scanning`, `no scanning required`, `not required`, `not needed`, `develop only`

Capital letters, dashes and spaces are ignored, so `No-Scan`, `NO SCANNING` and `no scan` all count.

This means a develop-only order whose option value is **No scanning required** will correctly *not* print your "SCAN WEB" line — you no longer have to write a separate condition for each spelling your products use.

* Note: If your lab uses wording that is not in the list above, write the condition against that wording directly, for example `{?option_group:scanning=web only:WEB:}`.

---

## Step 6 — Fallback text

The three printing tokens accept a fallback after a vertical bar:

```
{option_group_full:scanning|—}
```

This prints a dash when the job has nothing in that group, so your ticket never shows an awkward blank line.



---

## Good to know

* Two options in the same group on one job print **both** labels, comma separated, in the order set by **Sort order** in Option Display.
* `{option_group_full:...}` prints only one part when the other is blank, or when both are identical — you will not get a stray dash.
* Group changes apply to tickets generated from that point on. Tickets already produced are unchanged unless they are regenerated.
* Option Display only changes wording on screens and tickets. It never changes the original order information.

---

## Summary of Best Practices

1. Use one short, lower-case group name per real-world job step: `develop`, `scanning`, `prints`.
2. Map every option key that means that step into the same group, including new products as you add them.
3. Give every value a **Label shown** so tickets read cleanly instead of showing raw codes.
4. Use **Title shown for this value** when the heading itself needs to change, such as a scan resolution instruction.
5. Build a work-to-do block from `!=none` conditions so one layout serves every film product.
6. Add a fallback with `|` on any group that is not always present.
